gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a PlayStation 5 sends HDCP by default, so none of these recorders will record it until the shopper turns off "Enable HDCP" (AVerMedia gives the path as Settings > System). The same results also don't say that Xbox Series X|S and Switch drop HDCP once media apps are closed, or that a Blu-ray player's HDMI output always has HDCP and can't be recorded.
standout_why: I compared against the cited ClonerAlliance RecDual Dongle page, the cited UHD Pro product and knowledgebase pages, and the cited Hauppauge listing on streameez. I also tried the cited AVerMedia ER330 datasheet PDF, but its text could not be extracted. All three ChatGPT answers say only that HDCP-protected video "generally cannot be recorded." The RecDual page is the closest: it says "Any HDCP protected sources are NOT supported" and that the device has no HDR support ("turn off relevant settings from the video source"). Neither it nor any other rival page says which sources send HDCP by default or how to turn it off. They don't say that HDCP is on by default on PS5 but can be turned off, or that Blu-ray HDCP can't be turned off. They also don't say that UHD Pro records only in SDR, so an HDR source has to be turned off at the console.
decides: This doesn't change the ranking. Each maker says in its own words that its recorder won't record HDCP: Zowietek says "ZowieREC does not support HDCP", the ER330 page says "does not support viewing/recording/streaming of HDCP protected signals", and the RecDual page says "Any HDCP protected sources are NOT supported". The fix is on the source, not the recorder. A PS5, Xbox, Switch or camera works with any pick once HDCP is off on the PS5 and HDR is turned off. A Blu-ray player or a streaming app won't record on any of them. So the page should give the PS5 HDCP and HDR steps, and should not promise disc or streaming recording.

findings.label: PS5 HDCP default and how to turn it off
findings.value: HDCP is on by default; Settings > System, turn off "Enable HDCP"
findings.source_title: AVerMedia FAQ: What is HDCP and how could I fix HDCP message appear on my preview?
findings.note: AVerMedia lists this under PlayStation 4/5. It is a maker FAQ written for AVerMedia capture hardware generally, not a page for one model.

findings.label: Sony on capture devices with PS5
findings.value: "PS5 will allow the use of external HDMI-based capture devices by disabling HDCP in the Settings menu."
findings.note: Sony's own wording, from a 2020 launch FAQ. It doesn't give the menu path; the path above is AVerMedia's.

findings.label: Sources that always carry HDCP
findings.value: Blu-ray players/recorders: HDMI output is always HDCP-protected and can't be captured. PS3: HDCP is on for all HDMI output and can't be turned off in the menu. Netflix and Disney+ can't be captured whatever the settings.
findings.source_title: AVerMedia FAQ: What is HDCP and how could I fix HDCP message appear on my preview?

findings.label: Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch HDCP
findings.value: Closing media apps should disable HDCP; if it stays on, restart the console
findings.source_title: AVerMedia FAQ: What is HDCP and how could I fix HDCP message appear on my preview?
findings.note: These consoles have no HDCP toggle in this guidance; HDCP turns on only when a media app is open.

Sony's own PS5 menu path for 'Enable HDCP': the old manuals.playstation.net user-guide URL redirects to playstation.com/help, and the playstation.com support search found the setting only for PS4. The path comes from AVerMedia's FAQ; Sony's own wording is limited to the 2020 PS5 FAQ.

ClonerAlliance UHD Pro's own HDCP statement: none on the UHD Pro product page or knowledgebase overview. 'HDCP protected sources are NOT supported' shows up only in search results for the UHD Pro Max page and the Box Pro Pocket guide; I did not open those pages.
Hauppauge HD PVR Pro 60 HDCP and standalone-mode requirements: the cited streameez page gives only the title and $129.90; I did not open a Hauppauge spec page.
